articles.headline: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
articles.originalSnippet: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

facts: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’.
This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026.

Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions.

After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:                  the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit.
the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline.
The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1496
analysisOrUncertainties: Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.

facts: Data on sectoral deployment of bank credit for the month of September 2026, collected from 41 select scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), which together account for about 95 per cent of the total non-food credit by all SCBs1, are set out in Statements I and II.

On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit2  grew by 19.1 per cent as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, compared to 11.2 per cent during the corresponding fortnight of the previous year (i.e., October 03, 2025).

Highlights of the sectoral deployment of bank credit as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, are given below:                  Credit to agriculture and allied activities registered a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent vis-a-vis 8.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year.
Credit to industry recorded a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent (7.7 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of last year).
While credit to ‘large’ and ‘medium’ industries grew at an accelerated pace, ‘micro and small’ industries exhibited steady growth.

Among major industries, credit to ‘infrastructure’, ‘basic metal and metal products’, ‘all engineering’, ‘chemical and chemical products’, ‘food processing’ and ‘textiles’ marked buoyant y-o-y growth.

Credit to services sector registered a y-o-y growth of 28.3 per cent (9.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year), supported by buoyant growth in segments such as ‘non-banking financial companies’ (NBFCs), ‘trade’ ‘commercial real estate’, ‘transport operators’ and ‘professional services’.
Credit to personal loans segment recorded a y-o-y growth of 17.3 per cent, as compared with 11.5 per cent a year ago.
While credit growth in segments such as ‘housing’ and ‘vehicle loans’ remained resilient, ‘advances against fixed deposits’ accelerated.
Growth in ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘education’ decelerated compared to last year, albeit it remained strong.

Ajit Prasad                Deputy General Manager      (Communications)        Press Release: 2026-2027/1412        1 Data pertain to the last reporting fortnight of the month, based on sector-wise and industry-wise bank credit (SIBC) return.
With effect from December 31, 2025, definition of last reporting fortnight has been changed to the last day of the month under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act 2025.

Accordingly, the y-o-y growth rates from December 2025 onwards are based on end-of-month data for the current year and data for the last reporting fortnight (as per old definition) for the corresponding month of the previous year.
2 Non-food credit data are based on Section-42 return which covers all scheduled commercial banks (SCBs).

facts: Data on lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) (excluding regional rural banks and small finance banks) received during October 2026 are set out in Tables 1 to 9.

Highlights:     Lending Rates:                  The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on outstanding rupee loans of SCBs remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent in September 2026 compared to August 2026.
The WALR on fresh rupee loans of SCBs declined to 8.51 per cent in September 2026 from 8.61 per cent in August 2026.
1-Year median Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) of SCBs declined to 8.55 per cent in October 2026 from 8.61 per cent in September 2026.
The WALR on fresh as well as outstanding rupee loans exhibited a mixed movement across sectors in September 2026.

Deposit Rates:                  The weighted average domestic term deposit rate (WADTDR) on outstanding rupee term deposits of SCBs marginally declined to 6.55 per cent in September 2026 from 6.56 per cent in August 2026.
The WADTDR on fresh rupee term deposits of SCBs declined to 5.61 per cent in September 2026 from 5.67 per cent in August 2026.

facts: Government of India (GoI) has announced the sale (re-issue) of two dated securities for a notified amount of ₹36,000 crore as per the following details:                        Sr No          Security          Date of Repayment          Notified Amount             (₹ Crore)          GoI specific Notification          Auction Date          Settlement Date                          1          7.06% GS 2041          Jul 27, 2041          23,000          F.No.4(1)-B(W&M)/2026 dated          November 02, 2026          November 06, 2026            (Friday)          November 09, 2026            (Monday)                          2          7.43% GS 2076          Jan 19, 2076          13,000                                     Total                     36,000                                               2.
GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against each security mentioned above.3.
The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001.
The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.4.
The auction will be conducted using multiple price method.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 06, 2026 (Friday).
The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 09, 2026 (Monday).5.
Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m.
up to 09:30 a.m.
on November 06, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).6.
The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 03, 2026 – November 06, 2026.7.

Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.Ajit Prasad            Deputy General Manager  (Communications)    Press Release: 2026-2027/1424ANNEX Type of Auction1.
For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security.
For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.2.
The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.3.
In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued.
At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.Minimum Bid Size4.
The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.Non-Competitive Segment5.

In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities.
Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).6.

Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).7.

Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.Submission of Bids8.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).9.
Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure10.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted.

Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.11.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).12.
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).Multiple Bids13.
An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).14.
The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.Decision Making Process15.
On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.16.
Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.17.
Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.Issue of Securities18.

Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.Periodicity of Interest Payment19.
Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities.
The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.Underwriting of the Government Securities20.

The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)21.

The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading22.

The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No.
RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.Investment by Non-Residents23.

Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

facts: In pursuance of the announcement made in the Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies dated October 7, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India announces the constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) against the backdrop of rapidly evolving financial markets and infrastructure.

The Committee will serve as a forum for structured engagement with market participants and stakeholders by the Reserve Bank on policy and operational matters related to money, government securities and foreign exchange markets as well as the respective derivative markets and infrastructure.
The Committee will be Chaired by the Deputy Governor (DG) in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department (FMRD) of the Reserve Bank of India.

The Committee will comprise the following external members:                  Shri Ananth Narayan, Former Whole Time Member, SEBI, and Professor of Practice, IIT Bombay;                     Shri Shamsher Singh, Chairman, Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India (FIMMDA) and Deputy Managing Director, State Bank of India;                    Shri Neeraj Gambhir, Executive Director, Axis Bank;                     Shri Shailendra Jhingan, Head, Treasury and Economic Research, ICICI Bank;                    Shri Aditya Bagree, Managing Director, Head (Markets), Citibank India;                    Shri Nand Kishore, Managing Director, Clearing Corporation of India Limited; and                     Shri Ridham Desai, Managing Director, Morgan Stanley India.

The Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets will be as under:                  Issues related to the functioning, efficiency, liquidity and resilience of the money, government securities, foreign exchange and related derivative markets, and identification of measures to deepen and broaden these markets.
Issues relating to trading, clearing, settlement, reporting and other market infrastructure, including the associated regulatory and operational frameworks.
Emerging policy and operational issues affecting financial markets, including implementation of RBI measures and identification of unintended market frictions.
Any specific market issues or macroeconomic considerations referred to the Committee by the Reserve Bank.
The meetings of the Committee will be convened at least once a quarter.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1436
analysisOrUncertainties: International and domestic developments, financial innovations, and emerging risks that may affect Indian financial markets.

facts: The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH).
The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched.

The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, across 19 cities, viz., Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram.

The survey seeks qualitative responses from households on price changes (general prices as well as prices of specific product groups) in the three months ahead as well as in the one year ahead period and quantitative responses on current, three months ahead and one year ahead inflation rates.
The results of this survey provide useful inputs for monetary policy.
The agency, M/s Hansa Research Group Pvt.
Ltd., Mumbai has been engaged to conduct the survey of this round on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India.
For this purpose, the selected households will be approached by the agency, and they are requested to provide their response.
Other individuals, who are not approached by the agency can also participate in this survey by providing their responses using the linked survey schedule.

In case of any query/clarification, kindly contact at the following address:    The Director, Division of Household Surveys, Department of Statistics and Information Management, Reserve Bank of India, C-8, 2nd Floor, Bandra- Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai-400 051; Phone: 022-2657 8398, 022-2657 8332;Please click here to send email.
Ajit Prasad                Deputy General Manager      (Communications)        Press Release: 2026-2027/1429

sectionE_TechAndAI.originalSnippet:
This article was first published on November 6, 1976.
Concorde arrives, softly, softly
by Mark Giles

sectionA_IndiaTop10.headline: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Upholds State Powers on SC/ST Sub-Classification with Strict Empirical Criteria
sectionA_IndiaTop10.originalSnippet: The Supreme Court ruled that state governments have the constitutional power to sub-classify Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to ensure affirmative action reaches the most disadvantaged, while mandating verifiable empirical data.
sectionA_IndiaTop10.summary: A landmark seven-judge Constitution Bench held by a 6:1 majority that states are competent to sub-classify reserved categories. The judgment mandates that any sub-classification must be based on objective empirical evidence of inadequate representation rather than political discretion.

facts: Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) for the month of September 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement1.
On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs’ credit registered a growth of 15.4 per cent in September 2026 as compared to 13.3 per cent a year ago.

Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended September 30, 2026, are given below:                        Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.8 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as against 5.2 per cent a year ago.
Credit growth in industry sector declined to 7.4 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as compared with 10.2 per cent in September 2025.
Within industry, credit growth in ‘infrastructure’ remained subdued.
Credit growth in services sector moderated to 17.3 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 from 23.0 per cent a year ago.
While credit to ‘commercial real estate’ marked buoyant expansion, ‘trade’ and ‘transport operators’ segments also witnessed higher credit growth.
Retail loans growth accelerated to 21.9 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 compared to 16.8 per cent a year ago.
Within retail sector, ‘housing loans’, ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘vehicle loans’ witnessed accelerated credit growth.
Ajit Prasad            Deputy General Manager  (Communications)    Press Release: 2026-2027/14611 Provisional data as reported on the last day of the month.

Sectoral credit data of NBFCs are based on sample of (i) NBFCs in Upper and Middle Layers, and (ii) HFCs, accounting for about 87 per cent of total credit with respect to data published in ‘Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25’ (RTP 2024-25, outstanding as on September 2025).

facts: Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-261  round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment.

The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports.

The variations in outstanding foreign assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements.

Key highlights:                  Of the total number of Indian entities reporting foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or overseas direct investment (ODI), around 97 per cent entities were unlisted as at end-March 2026, and also held a major share in total FDI equity capital (at face value) in India (Tables 1 and 2A).
Non-financial companies accounted for more than 90 per cent of the FDI equity at face value (Table 2B).

In terms of market value, listed and unlisted companies had almost equal share in total FDI equity capital as at end-March 2026, however, 96.6 per cent of the FDI debt is held by unlisted companies (Table 3A).
In rupee terms, the ratio of inward FDI to ODI moderated to 4.2 times as on end-March 2026 from 5.5 times a year ago (Table 3B).

Other investment liabilities [viz., trade credit, loans, currency and deposits, and other payables with unrelated (third party) non-resident entities] recorded a growth of 11.9 per cent (y-o-y) in rupee terms as on end-March 2026; other investment assets with unrelated non-residents also rose by 16.1 per cent during the same period (Table 4).
The United States of America (16.5 per cent) followed by Mauritius (14.5 per cent), Singapore (13.7 per cent) and the United Kingdom (10.8 per cent) were the top sources of outstanding FDI.
In case of ODI, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America were the top destinations together accounting for more than 50 per cent share (Tables 5 and 6).
Manufacturing sector accounted for the highest share in the total outstanding FDI equity capital at market value (50.1 per cent), while 45 per cent share was held by services sector (Tables 7 and 8).

unitedStates.headline: Reuters: Global Semiconductor Equipment Billings Hit Record $31.8 Billion on Resilient AI Fab Demand
unitedStates.originalSnippet: Global billings for semiconductor manufacturing equipment climbed to $31.8 billion in the third quarter, driven by advanced packaging lithography and high-bandwidth memory expansions across Asia, Europe, and North America.
unitedStates.summary: Reuters reports that international semiconductor equipment spending reached unprecedented quarterly records. Advanced photolithography and wafer fabrication tools represent the fastest-growing capital investments as foundries scale high-bandwidth memory for artificial intelligence supercomputers.
unitedStates.whyItMatters: A core leading indicator of worldwide technology supply chain health, high-end electronics trade volumes, and chip manufacturing capital intensity.

corroboratingSources.headline: Global semiconductor tool makers report surging order backlogs for AI foundries
Chip equipment orders surge as global fabs compete for AI memory capacity

facts: Quarterly global equipment billings reached $31.8 billion, a 19% year-on-year increase.
Taiwan, China, and North America accounted for top regional capital tool installations.

unitedStates.headline: U.S. Clean Tech Manufacturing and Semiconductor Facility Construction Surpasses $220 Billion: CNN Special Report
unitedStates.originalSnippet: Data from the U.S. Census Bureau confirms non-residential industrial construction spending reached historic peaks, with over 150 gigafactories and advanced packaging fabs currently underway.
unitedStates.summary: A CNN economic investigation reveals that domestic manufacturing construction in the United States hit record annualized rates. Private semiconductor fabrication and battery production lines represent the largest share of private infrastructure growth.
unitedStates.whyItMatters: Demonstrates the durable structural realignment of critical hardware supply chains toward domestic and allied friend-shoring partners.

corroboratingSources.headline: Federal industrial subsidies drive surge in advanced domestic manufacturing plants

facts: Non-residential manufacturing construction rose 28% year-on-year.
High concentration of projects across Arizona, Ohio, Texas, and Georgia.
analysisOrUncertainties: High-skilled engineering labor shortages remain the main bottleneck for factory ramp-up timelines.

unitedStates.headline: CNN Exclusive: U.S. and International Tech Allies Finalise Historic Global Treaty on AI Safety Benchmarking
unitedStates.originalSnippet: Diplomats and computer science delegates from thirty nations signed the San Francisco Accord, inaugurating a shared red-teaming clearinghouse for autonomous AI agents.
unitedStates.summary: CNN reports from San Francisco that representatives from the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, India, and Japan signed a multilateral framework establishing standardized evaluation criteria for frontier AI models exceeding 10^26 FLOPs.
unitedStates.whyItMatters: Prevents fragmented regulatory divergence between Western tech ecosystems and fast-growing Global South tech centers, fostering unified safety verifications.

corroboratingSources.headline: International summit yields binding agreement on testing autonomous AI agents
US, UK, and allies sign milestone AI security verification treaty

facts: 30 countries established the International AI Safety Testing Network.
Mandatory pre-release evaluation protocols for next-generation frontier LLMs.
analysisOrUncertainties: Enforcement mechanisms rely on member state domestic export controls and cloud compute licensing.

unitedStates.headline: US Federal Reserve Cuts Benchmark Interest Rate by 25 Basis Points as Labor Market Softens and Inflation Moderates
unitedStates.originalSnippet: The Federal Reserve lowered its key interest rate by a quarter-point, continuing its recalibration toward a neutral policy stance.
unitedStates.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to lower the federal funds rate to a target range of 4.50% - 4.75%, noting that risks to achieving employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.
unitedStates.whyItMatters: Influences global capital flows, foreign institutional investor (FII) allocations into emerging markets like India, and US Dollar exchange rate movements.

corroboratingSources.headline: Fed cuts rates by 25 bps, sees steady path forward
US central bank makes second consecutive rate cut

facts: Federal funds rate reduced to 4.50% - 4.75%.
Fed Chair emphasized policy decisions will remain strictly meeting-by-meeting and data-dependent.
analysisOrUncertainties: Future pace of rate cuts depends on upcoming non-farm payroll and PCE price deflator readings.

unitedStates.headline: Trump’s war secretary Hegseth and Pacific Command chief Paparo may ‘soon visit China’
unitedStates.originalSnippet:
Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and US Pacific Command head Admiral Samuel Paparo may visit China “soon”, according to a veteran China hand.
Stephen Orlins, president of the non-profit organisation National Committee on United States-China Relations (NCUSCR), disclosed the potential visit during a video address at a conference on Friday in Sanya, in southern China’s Hainan province. More than 400 Chinese officials, foreign diplomats and legal experts have gathered in the South China Sea resort city.

sectionD_WorldEconomy.whyItMatters: Signals shifting macro conditions, interest rate trends, and financial market sentiment directly impacting consumer prices and domestic business investments.
facts: Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-261  round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment.

The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports.

The variations in outstanding foreign assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements.

Key highlights:                  Of the total number of Indian entities reporting foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or overseas direct investment (ODI), around 97 per cent entities were unlisted as at end-March 2026, and also held a major share in total FDI equity capital (at face value) in India (Tables 1 and 2A).
Non-financial companies accounted for more than 90 per cent of the FDI equity at face value (Table 2B).

In terms of market value, listed and unlisted companies had almost equal share in total FDI equity capital as at end-March 2026, however, 96.6 per cent of the FDI debt is held by unlisted companies (Table 3A).
In rupee terms, the ratio of inward FDI to ODI moderated to 4.2 times as on end-March 2026 from 5.5 times a year ago (Table 3B).

Other investment liabilities [viz., trade credit, loans, currency and deposits, and other payables with unrelated (third party) non-resident entities] recorded a growth of 11.9 per cent (y-o-y) in rupee terms as on end-March 2026; other investment assets with unrelated non-residents also rose by 16.1 per cent during the same period (Table 4).
The United States of America (16.5 per cent) followed by Mauritius (14.5 per cent), Singapore (13.7 per cent) and the United Kingdom (10.8 per cent) were the top sources of outstanding FDI.
In case of ODI, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America were the top destinations together accounting for more than 50 per cent share (Tables 5 and 6).
Manufacturing sector accounted for the highest share in the total outstanding FDI equity capital at market value (50.1 per cent), while 45 per cent share was held by services sector (Tables 7 and 8).

Temperatures approached 23C (73F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November.
The unseasonable warmth spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year.
The balmy conditions were caused by an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank.

This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average.Further south, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather affecting polling stations in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado.
The powerful thunderstorms even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing the relocation of a polling station.
The tornado caused extensive damage, although no causalities have been reported.
Officials across many states have requested federal funding assistance after the extreme weather resulted in widespread damage to homes and infrastructure.

Temperatures approached 23C (73F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November.
The unseasonable warmth spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year.
The balmy conditions were caused by an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank.

This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average.Further south, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather affecting polling stations in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado.
The powerful thunderstorms even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing the relocation of a polling station.
The tornado caused extensive damage, although no causalities have been reported.
Officials across many states have requested federal funding assistance after the extreme weather resulted in widespread damage to homes and infrastructure.

facts: The Reserve Bank of India, in exercise of its powers under Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, had superseded the Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd., Mumbai (the bank) for one year on November 24, 2023, due to material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The period of supersession was extended for a period of one-year, effective November 24, 2024 and further extended for a period of one year, effective November 24, 2025.

Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026.

Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise of its powers under sub-Section (1) of Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, has extended the period of supersession for a further period of one-year, effective from November 24, 2026.

Consequently, Shri Satya Prakash Pathak shall continue as the Administrator of the bank and shall be assisted by the present Committee of Advisors comprising of Shri Venkatesh Hegde, Shri Devendra Kumar, and Shri Suhas Gokhale.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1473

economyAndBusiness.summary: Government of India (GoI) has announced the sale (re-issue) of one dated security for a notified amount of ₹34,000 crore as per the following details:                        Sr No           Security           Date of Repayment           Notified Amount             (₹ Crore)           GoI specific Notificati...
economyAndBusiness.whyItMatters: Signals shifting macro conditions, interest rate trends, and financial market sentiment directly impacting consumer prices and domestic business investments.
facts: GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against the security mentioned above.
The security will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001.
The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
The auction will be conducted using multiple price method.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 13, 2026 (Friday).
The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 16, 2026 (Monday).
Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m.
up to 09:30 a.m.
on November 13, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The security will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 11, 2026 – November 13, 2026.
Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad                Deputy General Manager      (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1474            ANNEX      Type of Auction      1.
For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security.
For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued.
At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size      4.
The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment      5.

In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities.
Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids      8.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure      10.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted.

Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids      13.
An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process      15.
On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities      18.

Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment      19.
Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities.
The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities      20.

The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)      21.

The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading      22.

The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No.
RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents    23.

Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

facts: The Reserve Bank of India, in exercise of its powers under Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, had superseded the Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd., Mumbai (the bank) for one year on November 24, 2023, due to material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The period of supersession was extended for a period of one-year, effective November 24, 2024 and further extended for a period of one year, effective November 24, 2025.

Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026.

Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise of its powers under sub-Section (1) of Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, has extended the period of supersession for a further period of one-year, effective from November 24, 2026.

Consequently, Shri Satya Prakash Pathak shall continue as the Administrator of the bank and shall be assisted by the present Committee of Advisors comprising of Shri Venkatesh Hegde, Shri Devendra Kumar, and Shri Suhas Gokhale.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1473

The period of supersession was extended for a period of one-year, effective November 24, 2024 and further extended for a period of one year, effective November 24, 2025.

Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026.

Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise of its powers under sub-Section (1) of Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, has extended the period of supersession for a further period of one-year, effective from November 24, 2026.

Consequently, Shri Satya Prakash Pathak shall continue as the Administrator of the bank and shall be assisted by the present Committee of Advisors comprising of Shri Venkatesh Hegde, Shri Devendra Kumar, and Shri Suhas Gokhale.

facts: GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against the security mentioned above.
The security will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001.
The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
The auction will be conducted using multiple price method.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 13, 2026 (Friday).
The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m.
The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 16, 2026 (Monday).
Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m.
up to 09:30 a.m.
on November 13, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The security will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 11, 2026 – November 13, 2026.
Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad                Deputy General Manager      (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1474            ANNEX      Type of Auction      1.
For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security.
For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued.
At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size      4.
The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment      5.

In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities.
Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids      8.
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure      10.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted.

Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids      13.
An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process      15.
On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities      18.

Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment      19.
Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities.
The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities      20.

The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)      21.

The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading      22.

The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No.
RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents    23.

Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

courtsAndLegal.summary: A landmark seven-judge Constitution Bench held by a 6:1 majority that states are competent to sub-classify reserved categories. How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation?

The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society.

As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

facts: The Reserve Bank of India, in exercise of its powers under Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, had superseded the Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd., Mumbai (the bank) for one year on November 24, 2023, due to material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The period of supersession was extended for a period of one-year, effective November 24, 2024 and further extended for a period of one year, effective November 24, 2025.

Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026.

Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise of its powers under sub-Section (1) of Section 36AAA read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, has extended the period of supersession for a further period of one-year, effective from November 24, 2026.

Consequently, Shri Satya Prakash Pathak shall continue as the Administrator of the bank and shall be assisted by the present Committee of Advisors comprising of Shri Venkatesh Hegde, Shri Devendra Kumar, and Shri Suhas Gokhale.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1473

facts: Government of India announces the conversion/switch of its securities through auction for an aggregate amount of ₹25,000 crore (face value).

The security-wise details of the conversion/switch are given as under:                        Date of Auction          Source Securities          Amount (FV) of Source Securities            (in ₹ crore)          Destination Securities                          November 16, 2026            (Monday)          7.38% GS 2027            (Maturing on Jun 20, 2027)           5,000           7.18% GS 2037            (Maturing on Jul 24, 2037)                          8.26% GS 2027            (Maturing on Aug 02, 2027)           2,000           7.40% GS 2062            (Maturing on Sep 19, 2062)                          7.37% GS 2028            (Maturing on Oct 23, 2028)           4,000           6.83% GS 2039            (Maturing on Jan 19, 2039)                          7.26% GS 2029            (Maturing on Jan 14, 2029)           4,000           7.73% GS 2034            (Maturing on Dec 19, 2034)                          7.10% GS 2029            (Maturing on Apr 18, 2029)           5,000           6.64% GS 2035            (Maturing on Jun 16, 2035)                          7.04% GS 2029            (Maturing on Jun 03, 2029)           5,000           7.41% GS 2036            (Maturing on Dec 19, 2036)                          Total              25,000                          The market participants are required to place their bids in Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber) giving the amount of the source security and the price of the source and destination security expressed in Indian Rupees up to two decimal places.The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e., successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.Bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the e-Kuber platform on November 16, 2026 (Monday) between 10:30 AM and 11:30 AM.

The result of the auction will be announced on the same day and settlement will take place on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday).Government of India reserves the right to:      Accept offers for less than the notified amount.
Purchase marginally higher than the notified amount due to rounding-off effect.
Accept or reject any or all the offers either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.

Operational guidelines for switch transactions and other details are given in the Annex.Ajit Prasad            Deputy General Manager  (Communications)    Press Release: 2026-2027/1480AnnexOperational Guidelines for Switch/Conversion Transactions with the Government of IndiaSwitch module on e-Kuber1.
The market participants can bid in the switch auction through the Switch Transaction module provided in the e-Kuber portal.Bidding in a switch transaction2.

Bidding in the auction implies that the market participants agree to sell the source security/ies to the Government of India (GoI) and simultaneously agree to buy the destination security from the GoI at their respective quoted prices.Placing of bids3.
Each bid should specify the following details:      Amount of the source security (Face Value) that the participants are willing to sell.
Price of the source security (expressed up to two decimal places).
Choice of destination security and the price of the destination security (expressed up to two decimal places), at which the participants are willing to buy the destination security.

The participants can choose to bid for any/all the destination security/ies, but the aggregate amount of bids for the source security should not exceed their holdings of the source security in face value terms.
Minimum Bid size5.
Minimum bid size would be ₹10,000 and in multiples of ₹10,000 thereafter.
The participants are allowed to submit multiple bids.
However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted should not exceed the notified amount of source security/basket of source securities in the auction.
Price of source security6.
The price of the source security quoted must be equal to the FBIL closing price of the source security as on the previous working day.7.
Bids for source security not as per the price mentioned above will be rejected.
Price of destination security8.
Method of auction9.
The auction will be a multiple-price based auction, i.e.
successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted prices for the source and destination securities.Auction decision10.
The auction cut-off will be decided based on the price of the destination security/ies.11.
Successful bidders are those who have placed their bids at or above the cut-off price.
All bids lower than the cut-off price will be rejected.12.
There will be provision of pro-rata allotment, should there be more than one successful bid at the cut-off price.
Amount of destination security and dealing in odd amounts during switch auction13.
The switch ratio, which is the ratio of the price of the source security to the price of the destination security, would be rounded off at 8 decimal places.14.
The amount of destination security to be issued for each successful bid will be computed by multiplying the allotted amount (FV) of the source security with the rounded-off switch ratio.
The amount of destination security (FV) would be rounded-off to the nearest lower value in multiples of ₹10,000.

The odd amount of destination securities (less than ₹10,000) which has been rounded-off, would be notionally allotted and bought back from the bidders at the quoted bid price of the destination security.

The net cash consideration to be paid to the bidder for such odd amounts would be the clean price of these securities (as the accrued interest received during notional allotment and paid during notional buyback offset each other).
Fund settlement16.

Though the conversion would be broadly cash neutral, there will be fund settlement for the net accrued interest (accrued interest for the source security FV – accrued interest for the destination security FV) for each bid.
Cash consideration (due to rounding-off of face value of destination security) computed for each bid would be added to the net accrued interest.
Accordingly, fund settlement will be done for the final amount (Net accrued interest + cash consideration) for each bid.

Note: An illustration for the calculation of cash consideration due to rounding-off of destination security face value is as given below:       Amount of Source Security (FV)    ₹10,00,00,000.00        Price of Source Security     ₹97.50        Price of Destination Security     ₹99.20        Switch Ratio (rounded-off at 8 decimals)    0.98286290        Destination Security FV before rounding off     ₹9,82,86,290.00         Destination Security FV re-issued after rounding-off     ₹9,82,80,000.00         Odd amount of rounded-off destination security (FV)    ₹6290.00         Cash consideration due to rounding off (Clean Price calculated at the quoted price of destination security)     ₹6240.00   17.
The settlement of the auction would be held on T+1 basis.Help Desk 18.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 22705125).
analysisOrUncertainties: Bids for the destination security may be placed after taking into account the price of source security as mentioned above.

courtsAndLegal.summary: A landmark seven-judge Constitution Bench held by a 6:1 majority that states are competent to sub-classify reserved categories. courtsAndLegal.whyItMatters: Establishes constitutional doctrine on social justice jurisprudence, redefining state executive and legislative powers over reservation quotas across all Indian states.

facts: In terms of GOI notification F.No.4(22)-B(W&M)/2018 dated October 08, 2018 (SGB 2018-19 Series-III-Issue date November 13, 2018) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, the Gold Bond shall be repayable on the expiration of eight years from the date of issue of the Gold Bonds.
Accordingly, the final redemption date of the above tranche shall be November 13, 2026.

Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA).

Accordingly, the redemption price for final redemption due on November 13, 2026, shall be ₹14024/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand and Twenty-Four only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., November 10, November 11, and November 12, 2026.

facts: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’.
This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026.

Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions.

After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:                  the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit.
the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline.
The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers.
(Brij Raj)                 Chief General Manager    Press Release: 2026-2027/1496
analysisOrUncertainties: Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.

Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November.
A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours.

In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy.
This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera.
The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia.

Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November.
A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours.

In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy.
This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera.
The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia.
